name: Alaska

labor.name: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development

penalty.note: $25 for each year or part of a year delinquent; Alaska statutes also authorize an additional charge of 10% of the filing fee.
Penalty for failure to file a required biennial report.

entityTax: Corporate income tax (no individual income tax)

permitFee.note: The state has no statewide sales tax, so there is no sales tax permit fee.

salesTax.alternative: Alaska has no statewide sales tax; many boroughs and cities levy their own and sellers into Alaska register with the Alaska Remote Seller Sales Tax Commission (ARSSTC).

penalty.note: The state has no statewide sales tax, so there is no late sales tax return penalty.

unemployment.note: Employees also contribute; the 1.00% minimum applies to employers.
5% of the contributions due for each 30 days or fraction the report is late, with a $10 minimum and a 25% maximum.

newHire.note: No current official penalty amount for a late new hire report was found; secondary sources conflict or give only the federal $25 and $500 ceilings.

laborPosters.note: No penalty amount specific to the required workplace notices was found in the state's labor and workers' compensation sources.

workersComp.note: Civil penalty of up to $1,000 per uninsured employee per day of employment.

penalty.note: No separate state business-license late penalty is listed; a lapsed license may be renewed during the two-year lapse window, and after two years a new license is required.
